scope: Source-based editorial audit; implementation pending. Original/current full text and source statements are in inventory.json.

rooms.findingAndAction: Darkened room and northern door survive. Added hut/clearing detail is useful only if it avoids duplication; remove the unnecessary comma.
Original clearing/window/latch scene survives with a missing-word correction. Keep west/east paths but use natural low-comma sentences.
Original dark forest and distant river survive. Glinting water is modern embellishment; assess it openly rather than calling it archival. Keep useful exits once.
Original northward hut reference conflicts with the corrected map. Keep the western clearing and eastern slopes without a compressed destination list.
Glacial cliff and foot-beaten path survive. Keep the restored missing space. Change returns east to leads east if the exit sentence is needed.
Gioll and the east/west fork survive. The northward climb adds new information; retain it without an unnecessary connective comma.
Crater, slippery rim and rising vapour all survive. Keep the explicit fatal-west warning and safe east route as reaffirmed by the author.
Original height and distant bridge survive. Keep the distinction between seeing the bridge and reaching it; concise detour guidance must not repeat the same bearing.
Original arctic winds/cold survive. Mount spelling and comma-splice fix are reasonable. Describe western field and southern path in natural sentences.
Original precipice, Gioll, mountain and string bridge survive. The added north-return phrase repeats the mountain bearing; consolidate without losing southward crossing information.
Original creaking/swaying survives. Collapse warning is obsolete with the reusable bridge. Use the agreed north/south sentence and remove the redundant side-footing clause.
Original southern-bank sentence survives. Added north/west/east directions are useful new information but their comma-heavy list needs the author style pass.
Oak forest and poisonous mushrooms survive. Two modern route sentences can remain if clear and non-repetitive; remove unnecessary comma before and.
Basalt formation and VERY interesting cave survive. Northern exit addition must not assume the player arrived from the forest.
Original cliff view is expanded to a shelf on the southern bank. Keep physically clear positioning; remove return-language assumptions and excess punctuation.
Original sunlight and frightened aside survive. Outside route and need-for-light warning are useful approved additions; do not imply matches already exist.
Sacred Key clue survives. Earlier explorer attribution is an approved modern change. Keep a natural westward route without assuming prior visitation.
Original was only the generic dark-cavern sentence. Modern daylight/north and torture-chamber/west information adds orientation rather than replacing rich original prose.
Black elves, Svartalfheim and Viking dream survive. The westward exit is a useful addition; no abbreviated status sentence is needed.

Original small oak door locked from inside was replaced by formidable-door prose plus a terse status. Restore its meaning in natural closed-state sentences without the repeated east label. Open-state prose must not describe an intact door.
Original generic cavern was expanded. Remove north of the long tunnel from the opening. Introduce a long tunnel south and an oak doorway north without assuming prior visits.

Original corridor/breeze survives but its directional breeze changed. Call it a corridor as requested. West leads to a different cavern, not back to the entrance cavern. Keep south to torture chamber; no new eastern exit.
Original grotesque instruments, blood/bone and croaked-it voice survive with spelling/spacing fixes. Only clarify the modern eastern cavern destination and remove unnecessary comma.
Original north/south tunnel survives. Sealed was invented later. Author allows removal or improvement of the whole glowing-crack sentence; do not invent a puzzle or light source to explain it.
Original was generic dark cavern. Modern empty side-cave distinction and sole west exit are helpful; avoid back as an assumption if not needed.

Purple walls, chalk star, monks and ambiguous Norse-folk sentence are archival. Remove pagan. Reform the modern abbreviated exit list with a long tunnel and a passage towards the bat caves. Ask about the meaning of them before changing lore.
Original ledge/river and eastern exit survive. Balcony destination clarifies that exit. A northern passage is new useful information; prefer leads to a round chamber.

Original temple dedication/exile/End Of All Things survive in lightly rephrased form. Remove pagan. Rail is modern and necessary for the agreed rope action. Review the added west/below sentences for duplication and retain no automatic command coaching.

Original was generic dark cavern. Draught, junction and pillar are new navigation aids approved in the bat-loop simplification. Write full low-comma sentences and make the southern colony an immediate destination.
Original was generic dark cavern. Pillar and limestone chamber distinguish the modern reciprocal loop; do not claim the new details were archival.
Original was generic dark cavern. Dripping low passage is a new recognition cue; preserve the actual north/east connections in complete sentences.
The original renderer has no matching description for this room. Pale limestone is a modern landmark, not recovered lost text. Retain it as part of the approved simple loop.
Original bats, centuries of droppings and indescribable smell survive. Added commas are not needed for the original cadence. Keep genuinely new north/west route guidance.
Original was generic dark cavern. Key-chamber approach wording beyond the bat colony assumes an entry route; change to neutral location/visible connections.

Original statue imagery remains in the current paragraph. Locked gate became great gate plus an extra North gate locked/open fragment. Integrate locked/open wording into the original sentence and delete duplicate fragments. Balcony text must not assert every arrival was a descent.
Original was generic dark cavern. Shaft and river-sound directions clarify the lower region; avoid redundant bearings or a bare exit list.

rooms.disposition: Retain approved riddle change; review lost voice
rooms.findingAndAction: Original crypt/decay survives. APE riddle was deliberately replaced by VARD. The original monks-liked-silly-puzzles aside was lost too; consider recovering the aside only if it fits the approved clue. Do not restore APE mechanics.

Original cell survives. Closed western wall is obsolete. Preserve shaft/hatch information in natural prose; remove terse shaft and DROP command coaching from ordinary description while keeping fair physical clues.
Original was generic dark cavern. Shaft/cell and southern cavern directions are useful; avoid just beyond as an assumption about arrival.

Original ledge, subterranean river and roof inflow survive. Lower-region route additions are useful but currently rely on fragments and semicolon lists. Clarify in full sentences without inventing river flow directions.
Original drainage-network exclamation survives in rephrased form. Prefer its original voice with spacing correction where possible. Added conduit/junction directions are useful.

Original shared drainage surprise was replaced with a neutral introduction. Restore evocative wording where it helps, but do not mechanically repeat one exclamation in every drain. Keep distinctive route information.

Original shared drainage line replaced by a detailed junction. Keep approved physical hatch/latch clue and real paths. Remove unrequested automatic OPEN HATCH coaching from ordinary narrative if the latch is adequately described.
Original shared drainage line replaced by a blind-branch description. This is a useful modern distinction, not a lost rich individual scene. Keep a natural exit sentence.
Original waterfall/surface-Gioll sentence survives. Review repeated from phrasing only mechanically. New steps/safe paths should be complete sentences with no invented bearings.
Original was generic dark cavern. Pearl-white walls and a winding height-changing passage clarify the modern geography; do not replace with an abbreviated exit list.
Original staircase/southward direction survives. Current top-of-stairs and waterfall/east-chamber details add orientation. No need to remove useful atmosphere or bearings.
Original crumbling ledge, magic castle and conversational aside survive. Additional east crossing and northern route must not repeat the castle bearing or presume entry route.

Original drawbridge lowering by magic was replaced with golden-bridge and mechanical status prose. Preserve present crossing rules but consider restoring original magical voice rather than a technical crossing-secures explanation.
Courtyard WOW, really-something castle, inscription and escape tunnel survive. Added drawbridge/magazine directions need natural wording and restrained commas, not wholesale removal.
Original really-super-castle sentence survives. Westward courtyard guidance adds information; prefer leads rather than back if route-neutrality matters.
Original eastern bank survives. Old eastward cliff tunnel now leads north under the corrected map. Do not restore the wrong bearing; clarify underground river and wooden crossing naturally.

rooms.findingAndAction: Original wooden bridge survives with useful crossing/path directions. The archival renderer also prints generic dark cavern here; dropping that duplicate was a reasonable cleanup.
Original knee-deep freezing water survives with a missing-space fix. Keep the service path and new drains route, removing unnecessary connective comma and assumed known destinations.
